subject: Science & Technology
question: Mouse is
explanation: A computer mouse (plural mice or mouses) is a hand-held pointing device that detects two- dimensional motion relative to a surface. This motion is typically translated into the motion of a pointer on a display, which allows a smooth control of the graphical user interface of a computer. Credit of invention of the computer mouse goes to an American engineer Douglas Carl Engelbart.
source: Uttarakhand UDA/LDA (Pre) 2006 · General Science & Technology GS p.365

subject: Science & Technology
question: ROM is a-
explanation: Read-only memory (ROM) is a type of non- volatile memory used in computers and other electronic devices. Data stored in ROM cannot be electronically modified after the manufacture of the memory device. ROM is the permanent memory in computer and this can be used for reading only.
source: Uttarakhand Lower (Pre) 2016 · General Science & Technology GS p.368

subject: Science & Technology
question: LAN means
explanation: A local-area network (LAN) is a computer network that spans in a relatively small area. Most often, a LAN is confined to a single room, building or group of buildings, however, one LAN can be connected to other LAN over any distance via telephone lines and radio waves.
source: Uttarakhand UDA/LDA (M) 2007 · General Science & Technology GS p.374

subject: Science & Technology
question: CPU means
explanation: CPU is the abbreviation for Central Processing Unit. Sometimes refers to simply as the central processor, but more commonly called a processor, the CPU is the brains of the computer where most calculations takes place.
source: Uttarakhand Lower (Pre) 2011 · General Science & Technology GS p.383

subject: Science & Technology
question: IRC means
explanation: IRC (Internet Relay Chat) is a Protocol for real time text messaging between Internet connected computers created in 1988. It is mainly used for group discussion in chat rooms between two users, data transfer and various server-side and client side commands.
source: Uttarakhand UDA/LDA (M) 2007 · General Science & Technology GS p.383

question: When the alarm of your smart phone rings in the morning, you wake up and tap it to stop the alarm which causes your geyser to be switched on automatically. The smart mirror in your bathroom shows the day's weather and also indicates the level of water in your Science Technology 39 overhead tank. After you take some groceries from your refrigerator for making breakfast, it recognises the shortage of stock in it and places an order for the supply of fresh grocery items. When you step out of your house and lock the door, all lights, fans, geysers and AC machines get switched off automatically. On your way to office, your car warns you about traffic congestion ahead and suggests an alternative route, and if you are late for a meeting, it sends a- message to your office accordingly. In the context of emerging communication technologies, which one of the following term" best applies to the above scenario?
explanation: –(b) Internet of things refers to the interconnection via the Internet of computing devices embedded in everyday objects enabling them to send and receive data. Internet of Things include connected security systems, thermostats, cars, electronic appliances, lights in household and commercial environments, alarm clocks, speaker systems, vending machines and more.
source: UPSC IAS (Pre) G.S. 2018 · General Science & Technology GS p.387

subject: Science & Technology
question: Which one of the following approaches comes under the category of biotechnology?
options: Use of living organisms or substances obtained from them in industrial processes
Modernizing the commercial industries to produce products for use in biological research
Use of modern technology to investigate biological disorders
Use of industrial technology to increase the biosphere
explanation: (a) Biotechnology is the broad area of biology, involving living systems and organisms to develop or make products, or "any technological application that uses biological systems, living organisms, or derivatives thereof, to make or modify products or processes for specific use".
source: (IAS (Pre) G.S. 1993) · General Science & Technology GS p.401

subject: Science & Technology
question: What is the application of Somatic Cell Nuclear Transfer Technology?
options: Production of organisms free of diseases
explanation: –(c) Reproductive cloning of animals is application of Somatic Cell Nuclear Transfer Technology. In genetics and developmental biology, somatic cell nuclear transfer (SCNT) is a laboratory technique for creating an ovum with a donor nucleus. The nucleus of the somatic cell is then inserted into the enucleated egg cell. After being inserted into the egg, the somatic cell nucleus is reprogrammed by the host cell.
source: IAS (Pre) G.S.-Ist 2017 · General Science & Technology GS p.403
